content: The test image shows a corn ear with rotted kernels at the butt/tip end — pink/reddish discoloration, shrunken kernels, dark decay near the silk area. This is an ear rot. Let me compare the ear rot classes.

**Key observations from test image:**
- Corn ear with rot concentrated at the **tip/silk end**
- Kernels show **pink/reddish-brown discoloration**, some shrunken
- Dark black decay at the very tip junction
- Rest of ear healthy/yellow

**Comparison analysis:**
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White uniform mold covering entire ear from base — doesn't match
- **Ear_rots_Aspergillus**: Olive-green powdery mold — doesn't match
- **Fusarium**: Scattered pink "starburst" kernel infection pattern — doesn't fully match
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Starts at the TIP of the ear, pink/reddish mold — **matches the tip-end location and pink coloration**

The rot starting at the tip/silk end with pink-reddish kernel discoloration is the hallmark of Gibberella ear rot (*Fusarium graminearum*), which infects through the silk channel.
